items.title: Dave Pell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: And Ray Brown is playing the blues and they’re cooking, boy. And he said, “okay, Dave, let’s go.” And I get up and play

ctx.x: You know since we are on camera, can you explain this to our students? [hand gesture]

It’s in three flats because down is flats and if you are going to play in four sharps, like Lester, or seven sharps like Lester, he always did that kind of number, so you’d figure in all the sharps and then flat the fifth. And there’s a story about Ray Brown. We were doing a show one day and they were playing the blues, we were not even paying attention. And they’re playing the blues, while the cameras are being set up, the bands always used to do films you know and things like that. And Ray Brown is playing the…
horns to play in. And Lester did that on purpose. Half the time he played “Lady Be Good”, no, no, “let’s play it up a tone,” and oh, everybody else around him died.
